    AI Overview
    Cancer is a group of diseases characterized by uncontrolled cell growth caused by DNA alterations, often forming tumors or spreading via the bloodstream/lymph system. Diagnosis involves physical exams, imaging, and lab tests, while treatments typically include surgery, chemotherapy, and immunotherapy. Prevention focuses on reducing risk factors like smoking, poor diet, and alcohol. 
    Key Aspects of Cancer 
    • Definition & Types: Cancer occurs when abnormal cells divide without control, invading nearby tissues. Main types include carcinomas (skin/tissue lining), sarcomas (bone/connective tissue), and leukemia/lymphoma (blood/immune system).
    • Causes & Risks:
      Cancer results from gene alterations (DNA changes) that can be inherited or caused by environmental exposures, such as tobacco (leading cause), UV radiation, and certain infections.
    • Diagnosis Methods: Early detection is crucial, often found through physical exams, imaging tests (CT, MRI), and laboratory tests, such as blood, urine, or tumor marker tests.
    • Treatment Options: Common treatments include surgery to remove tumors, radiation therapy, chemotherapy (using drugs to kill cells), and newer methods like immunotherapy, which boosts the body's natural defenses.
    • Latest Advancements & Trends: Research is focusing on targeted therapies that attack specific genetic changes, personalized immunotherapies (like CAR-T cell therapy), and improving early detection methods. 
    Global Burden & Prevention 
    • Statistics: In 2022, there were roughly 20 million new cases and 9.7 million deaths worldwide. By 2050, cases are expected to reach 33 million per year.
    • Prevention: Up to 50% of cancer deaths are preventable, primarily by avoiding tobacco, maintaining a healthy weight, and limiting alcohol.

    People also ask
    What are the 7 warning signs of cancer?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    The seven warning signs of cancer, often summarized by the acronym CAUTION (by the American Cancer Society), include changes in bowel/bladder habits, sores that do not heal, unusual bleeding/discharge, thickening or lumps, indigestion/difficulty swallowing, obvious changes to moles/warts, and a nagging cough or hoarseness. Persistent symptoms lasting over two weeks should be evaluated by a healthcare professional. 
    Key Cancer Warning Signs (CAUTION Mnemonic) 
    • Change in bowel or bladder habits (e.g., chronic constipation, diarrhea, or pain).
    • A sore that does not heal (skin or mouth sores that linger).
    • Unusual bleeding or discharge (e.g., blood in stool/urine, abnormal vaginal bleeding)
      .
    • Thickening or lump in the breast, testicles, or elsewhere.
    • Indigestion or difficulty in swallowing.
    • Obvious change in a wart or mole (size, color, shape, or thickness).
    • Nagging cough or hoarseness that persists. 
    Additional Important Warning Signs 
    • Unexplained Weight Loss: Losing 10 pounds or more without trying.
    • Persistent Fatigue: Extreme tiredness that does not improve with rest.
    • Persistent Fever or Night Sweats: Often linked to blood cancers.
    • Chronic Pain: New or worsening pain in bones or other areas.
    • Skin Changes: Darkening, yellowing (jaundice), or new redness. 
    If you experience these symptoms, especially if they are persistent or worsening, it is important to contact a doctor for evaluation.
